newsitem.title: USA: Shuttle Discovery takes off on schedule.
newsitem.headline: Shuttle Discovery takes off on schedule.

text.p: The space shuttle Discovery lit up the Florida night sky on Tuesday as it blasted off on a mission to refurbish the Hubble Space Telescope.
The $2 billion reusable spaceship lifted off from Florida's Kennedy Space Center at 3:55 a.m. EST (8:55 GMT), beginning a two-day chase through space to catch the orbiting observatory.
During the 10-day mission, the shuttle crew planned to make four spacewalks to install two new scientific instruments aboard the telescope and refurbish various aging components.

It will be the first time astronauts have visited Hubble since a 1993 repair mission corrected its blurred vision. The observatory was launched in 1990 and was designed to receive periodic visits from the space shuttle for routine maintanence and instrument upgrades.

The astronauts will treat the telescope with the greatest of care to avoid damaging its fragile solar panels. Astronomers said the possible risks were outweighed by the scientific rewards of the refurbishment.
The shuttle crew of seven was led by Kenneth Bowersox. Pilot was Scott Horowitz and mission specialists are Mark Lee, Gregory Harbaugh, Steve Hawley, Joe Tanner and Steve Smith.
